item.title: The science behind the 'super-ager' brain
item.description: Scientists at the University of Illinois College of Medicine Chicago found that “SuperAgers” generate twice as many new neurons in the hippocampus.

item.title: Kim Jong Un fuels succession buzz with daughter's matching leather jacket
item.description: As Kim Jong Un affirms his authority over North Korea at a rare party congress, speculation is growing that his teenage daughter Ju Ae is closer to being named his successor.

item.title: Plaintiff begins testimony in social media addiction trial
item.description: The plaintiff in the social media addiction trial, a 20-year-old woman identified by the initials K.G.M., has begun her testimony in the landmark case. NBC News' Steve Patterson and Danny Cevallos have details on what she has said about her social media use and what the attorneys for the companies will be watching for before beginning their side of questions.

item.title: 'Nearly blind' refugee found dead after being released by Border Patrol in N.Y.
item.description: A nearly blind refugee who didn’t speak English was found dead in New York state days after he was left at a coffee shop by Customs and Border Protection officers, according to authorities

item.title: Church congregant sues alleged Minnesota church protesters
item.description: A St. Paul, Minnesota, church member has filed a federal lawsuit alleging that a group of people, including journalist Don Lemon and activist Nekima Levy Armstrong, unlawfully disrupted a service last month as part of a coordinated political demonstration

item.title: Prosecutor says he knew charges against Kilmar Abrego Garcia would likely be seen as vindictive
item.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, whose mistaken deportation has galvanized both sides of the immigration debate, claims that the criminal prosecution is vindictive.

item.title: Columbia University student released from ICE detention with help of Mamdani
item.description: A Columbia University student was released from ICE detention after her arrest, which led to massive protests at the school. NBC News’ Monica Alba explains how New York City Mayor Mamdani aided in her release.

item.title: Pakistan is in 'open war' with Afghanistan, its defense minister says
item.description: PESHAWAR, Pakistan — Pakistan and Afghanistan traded cross-border attacks overnight, government officials from both countries confirmed to NBC News on Friday, alleging heavy losses on both sides as Pakistan’s defense minister declared “open war” between the two South Asian nations

item.title: American citizen among victims in Cuba boat shooting, U.S. officials say
item.description: According to two U.S. officials, at least one U.S. citizen was killed and another injured after a 24-foot boat allegedly exchanged gunfire with Cuban border patrol. NBC News’ Jose Diaz-Balart reports.

item.title: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton testifies in Epstein investigation
item.description: Hillary Clinton said she told lawmakers that she did not know Jeffrey Epstein, and never went to his home or his island. The Clintons have repeatedly denied wrongdoing and have not been accused of any crimes related to Epstein. NBC News’ Ryan Nobles reports.
